description: Retrieve readable OCR DjVuTXT or plain text from an Internet Archive item, including public-domain books, documents, scanned periodicals, and transcripts. Each call reads one text file: the one file names, or by default the first DjVuTXT file (else Text, Plain Text, or another .txt file). An item can hold several, such as one per volume; a notice then gives the count. Set max_chars for page size, then pass next_continuation as continuation with the same identifier and omit char_offset. Direct char_offset access remains available. To jump to a passage, pass find with a phrase: the page starts at its first match at or after char_offset or the continuation's position, and match_offset reports where; that page's next_continuation, passed back with the same find, searches on from the page's end. To list the DjVuTXT files of an item, call ia_get_item with format "DjVuTXT".

char_offset.description: Character offset to start reading from (default 0); with find, where the search starts. For sequential pages use next_continuation as continuation instead. Omit char_offset when using continuation.

continuation.description: Opaque next_continuation from the previous page. Omit char_offset when using it; blank is omitted.

file.description: The text file to read, named exactly as ia_get_item lists it, e.g. "Strabo 02 Geography 3-5_djvu.txt". It must be readable text: format DjVuTXT, Text, or Plain Text, or a .txt name whose format is not Metadata. Omit to read the default: the first DjVuTXT file, else Text, else Plain Text, else another .txt file. With continuation, omit it or name the file the continuation reads; blank is omitted.

find.description: A literal phrase of at most 500 characters to find in the file read; the page then starts at its first match at or after char_offset or the continuation's position. Letters match regardless of case, one character to one (ß never matches ss); a whitespace run in the phrase matches any whitespace run in the text, line breaks included; every other character matches itself. OCR misreads and words hyphenated across line ends break a phrase, so prefer a short, distinctive one. Blank is omitted.

identifier.description: Internet Archive item identifier, e.g. "prideprejudice00aust" (Pride and Prejudice), from ia_search_items results; or an archive.org item URL, such as https://archive.org/details/prideprejudice00aust or its download, stream, metadata, or embed form, read as the identifier it names. A download, stream, or storage-node URL naming a file reads that file when file is omitted.

max_chars.description: Maximum number of characters to return in this response. Defaults to the server-configured maximum (IA_MAX_SNAPSHOT_CHARS, typically 50 000); a larger value is served at that maximum, with a notice. Lower values reduce token usage.

name: ia_get_text

char_offset.description: Character offset used for this response: with find, where its first match begins (equal to match_offset), or where the search started when nothing matched.

error.description: Present when the call failed. Absent on success.

code.description: JSON-RPC error code for this failure.

reason.description: Machine-readable failure mode. Declared by this tool: `invalid_continuation`: A continuation is unknown, expired, belongs to another item, reads a different file than file names, or its file changed. `range_unavailable`: The download ignored or returned an invalid conditional byte range. `ambiguous_pagination`: Both a nonblank continuation and char_offset were supplied. `find_incomplete`: With find, the search stopped before the download's request timeout or the call deadline would have cut it off, once past its start, or at a later char_offset it reached with a continuation stored there; or the first match was found past a whitespace run longer than the text one call holds, so the call names the match's char_offset instead of returning its page. `item_not_found`: The identifier does not exist in the Internet Archive. `invalid_identifier`: identifier holds "/" or ":" but is not an archive.org item URL: a URL on another site, a Wayback Machine capture, or an archive.org page that names no item. `invalid_file`: file, or the file a download, stream, or storage-node URL names, is not in the item manifest or is not readable text. `no_text_file`: The item exists but lists no readable text file: no DjVuTXT, Text, or Plain Text file, and no .txt file other than Metadata sidecars. `download_forbidden`: Access to this item is restricted — it is in a login-required or limited collection. `archive_unavailable`: The Internet Archive Metadata API or the text file download did not answer within the request timeout or the call's 55 s deadline (the request timeout when that is longer), could not be reached, answered HTTP 5xx after retries, 429, or another 4xx, or the metadata response was unreadable; or, with find, the download was too slow for the search to get past its start before then. Other values are possible when a failure originates below the handler.

recovery.description: Actionable next step for the caller.

message.description: Human-readable description of what went wrong.

has_more.description: True when there is more text beyond this slice. Use next_continuation, or add max_chars to char_offset if no token is available.

match_offset.description: With find, the character offset where its first match begins, equal to char_offset. Omitted when find matched nothing or was not given.

max_chars.description: Maximum characters this response could hold — the requested max_chars, or the server maximum when the request exceeded it.

next_continuation.description: Opaque next-page token; use as continuation with the same identifier and omit char_offset. Expires after one hour.

notice.description: Explains a max_chars clamp or why efficient continuation is unavailable, with the next char_offset or end-of-document status; that find matched nothing from char_offset to the end of source_file; or — when file was omitted — how many readable text files the item holds and how to list them.

source_file.description: Filename of the source text file fetched from the item.

source_file_bytes.description: Size of the source text file in bytes, from the item manifest — a byte count, not a character count (non-ASCII text takes several bytes per character). Omitted when the manifest lists no size.

text.description: The text slice starting at char_offset up to max_chars characters.

title: Get Internet Archive Item Text
